context: Norsund ("north-tongue") is the common language of Thiolden. This file is the authoritative list of its sounds and sound rules.
The machine-readable blocks (inventory, onsets, codas) are read by tools/norsund to validate new words.
IPA is given between slashes for phonemes and square brackets for actual pronunciations.

diphthongs.note: written ay at the end of a word (nay, Thiolnay); a stem keeps ay before suffixes (Vilnayan)

reduced_vowel.note: allophone of e in an unstressed final syllable; see PHON-06

rules.title: Twenty consonants, six vowels
rules.rule: Norsund has 20 consonants and 6 vowel qualities (a e i o u y), each of which can be long (written double). There are three diphthongs: ei/ay, au and ou. The letters c, q, x and z are not used.

rules.title: Stress
rules.rule: Native words are stressed on the first syllable. Compounds take primary stress on the first element and one secondary stress on the first syllable of the next element (none if that element starts at the second syllable). Learned Kedre loans (layer kedre-learned) keep Kedre's stress on the second-to-last syllable.

rules.title: Syllable shape
rules.rule: The syllable is (C)(C)(C)V(C)(C)(C). Allowed onsets and codas are listed above. "ng" never starts a word; h, j and w never end a syllable; kj and gj never end a word. Double consonants (geminates) occur only after a vowel, never at the start of a word.

rules.title: The th sound
rules.rule: th is [θ] (thin) at the start of a word and next to voiceless consonants, and [ð] (this) between vowels and after a vowel at the end of a word. In Starisund (Auristar) it is [s] everywhere.

rules.title: Glides from i and u
rules.rule: An unstressed i before another vowel in the same syllable is the glide [j]; an unstressed u before a vowel is [w]. The stressed vowel is the second one.

rules.title: Reduction of final e
rules.rule: The letter e in an unstressed final syllable is pronounced [ə] (the a in "sofa"). This applies to each element of a compound separately and to all inflectional endings (-en, -er, -ene, -ade, -de).

rules.title: Nasal assimilation
rules.rule: n before k or g is pronounced [ŋ].

rules.title: Long consonants
rules.rule: Written double consonants are held long in common Norsund and Old Norsund. Starisund shortens them in speech but keeps the double spelling.

rules.title: r
rules.rule: r is a tap [ɾ] between vowels and a trill [r] elsewhere. It is never the English glide.

rules.title: Starisund accent
rules.rule: The Auristar accent applies three Venetian-style changes in speech only: th becomes [s], word-final n becomes [ŋ], and double consonants are short. Saying "Thiolden" as [ˈsjol.dəŋ] marks a city speaker.

rules.title: English-friendly readings
rules.rule: For voice work, y may be read as "ee" with rounded lips, kj as "ky", and r as a light tap. Never read j as in "jam", g as in "gem", s as "z", or a as in "cat". See docs/languages/norsund/pronunciation-guide.md.

context: The standard romanization is plain ASCII so that every contributor can type it. One spelling stands for one sound.
Native scripts (runes and Lysrit) are documented in records/languages/scripts.

rules.title: Letters
rules.rule: Norsund is written with a b d e f g h i j k l m n o p r s t u v w y and the digraphs th, kj, gj, ng. No accents, no apostrophes, no c, q, x or z. Dictionaries sort the digraphs as separate letters, in the order given above (so kjold comes after kyr).

rules.title: ei and ay
rules.rule: The diphthong /ej/ is written ei inside a word and ay at the end of a word. A stem that ends in ay keeps it when suffixes are added.

rules.title: Compounds
rules.rule: Compounds are written as one word. Where two elements meet and the letters would be misread as a digraph (n+g, t+h, k+j, g+j), write a hyphen: nim-gand, not nimgand. Three identical consonants in a row reduce to two (kull + land = kulland).

rules.title: Capital letters
rules.rule: Capitalize proper names, gods, peoples and demonyms (Thiolnay, Aurinay), languages (Norsund, Kedre), titles used with a name (Lys Thrimde), and the first word of a sentence. Ordinary nouns, days and months are lower-case.

rules.title: Foreign names
rules.rule: Names from other languages keep their own spelling (Karhak'Modan, Kyr Thor'Vale, Luxis). An apostrophe in such a name must stand for a real sound in that language (records/languages/languages.yaml lists what each one marks). When such a name is fully absorbed into Norsund it is respelled (Kedre murra became Norsund mur).

rules.title: Standard spellings of canon names
rules.rule: Where lore records spell a name in more than one way, the standard Norsund spelling is the first listed: Midelmar (not Middlemar), Haakon (not Hakkon), Volggan (not Vloggan, Vlogan), Vairean (adjective of Vaire; not Varian), Rechtar (not Rechatar). The lore records were corrected to these spellings on 2026-11-19.

rules.title: Scholarly spelling of Old Norsund
rules.rule: When quoting Old Norsund, scholars may use þ for th, ð for th between vowels, and an acute accent for long vowels (Old Norsund þjol). Reconstructed Proto-Norsund and Proto-Valian forms are starred and written in IPA-like letters (*kjoldu, *geldhu). The modern standard never uses these letters.

rules.title: th + j is written thi
rules.rule: The glide [j] after th is written i, because "thj" looks odd to English readers: thiol /θjol/, thiarka /ˈθjar.ka/. After every other consonant it is written j (kjold, Starifjolden, hjalda).

rules.title: Punctuation
rules.rule: Latin punctuation as in English. In verse, a raised dot (·) may separate the two half-lines. Evidential particles are set off with a comma: Tyr kjoldade murin, sa.

context: Glosses follow the Leipzig Glossing Rules. AN = animate, IN = inanimate, DEF = definite, GEN = genitive.

morphology.stem_final_e: When a stem ends in unstressed -e, the e of a suffix that begins with e or a is dropped (rie + ar = rier, rie + in = rien).
morphology.stem_final_a: When a stem ends in -a, a suffix that begins with a drops that a (kelda + ar = keldar, kelda + arne = keldarne).

after_vowel.note: After a stem ending in a vowel other than unstressed e, definite -in becomes -n (nay + in = nayn); plurals keep their full form (nay + en = nayen).

rules.title: Two noun classes
rules.rule: Every noun is animate (people, gods, spirits, beasts and other living beings) or inanimate (everything else). Class is fixed in the dictionary and decides the plural. In Starisund, stars, constellations and the Auristar itself are animate; in common Norsund and Old Norsund they are inanimate.

rules.title: Plural
rules.rule: Animate nouns add -en; inanimate nouns add -ar. Stems in unstressed -e drop the suffix vowel.

rules.title: Umlaut plurals
rules.rule: Six very old animate nouns form the plural by changing the vowel instead of adding -en: lud/lyd, thamm/themm, gat/get, fuld/fyld, tunn/tynn, brod/bred. They are leftovers of a Proto-Norsund plural -iz that changed the vowel (umlaut) and was then lost. Their definite plurals add -ene to the changed vowel (lydene, "the people"). Hand, foot and tooth are animate for historical reasons only.

rules.title: The definite suffix
rules.rule: "The" is a suffix: -in in the singular, -ene (animate) or -arne (inanimate) in the plural. After a vowel the singular is -n. There is no word for "a"; a bare noun is indefinite. The number yn "one" can mean "a certain".

rules.title: Genitive
rules.rule: Possession is marked with -i after a consonant and -s after a vowel, on the last word of the possessor noun (after any plural or definite suffix). The possessor comes first. A possessed noun takes no definite suffix: the possessor already makes it definite.

rules.title: No other cases
rules.rule: Subjects and objects are not marked on nouns; word order (see Syntax) and pronoun forms show who does what. Old Norsund had four cases, which survive only in set phrases and in the archaic register.

rules.title: Mass nouns
rules.rule: Nouns for substances (ylv "water", aul "ale", grjot "stone" as material) have no plural unless they mean kinds or portions.

rules.title: Honorific vocative
rules.rule: In Starisund, a title used to address someone takes -a: Lysa! ("O Light!"), Kyra! ("O Blade!"), Fyra! (to a tavern cook, "O Fire!"). Ordinary names are not changed.

rules.title: Theology in the grammar
rules.rule: Because stars are animate in Starisund, an Aurinay says staren ("the stars", as beings) and uses the animate pronoun sel for a star. Country speech says starar and at. Using the inanimate forms in an Auristar temple is a known faux pas.

morphology.adverb_epenthesis: et (used when -t would make a coda not allowed by grammar/01: lang > langet, gorm > gormet)

rules.title: Position and form
rules.rule: Adjectives come before the noun and never change for number or definiteness.

rules.title: Predicate adjectives
rules.rule: After the copula vesa the adjective is unchanged. In mottos, inscriptions and poetry (the "carved style") the present copula is left out.

rules.title: Adjectives as nouns
rules.rule: Any adjective can name a person or thing with that quality. It then takes noun endings, animate by default: thiol-in "the brave one", thiol-en "brave ones", thiol-ene "the brave ones".

rules.title: Comparison
rules.rule: Comparative -ar, superlative -ast; "than" is thon; "as ... as" is sam ... sam. Four common adjectives are irregular (table above). In Auristar the superlative is folk-etymologized as "starred".

rules.title: Adverbs
rules.rule: Adverbs of manner add -t to the adjective (thiolt "bravely", vilt "freely"); where -t would make an illegal word ending, they add -et instead (lang > langet). Intensifier ful "very" goes before the adjective or adverb. Hel "good" has the adverb helt "well".

rules.title: Adjectives from nouns
rules.rule: -a "of, belonging to" (Vilnaya "of the free folk"), -ug "full of, -y" (starug "starry"), -nuth "without, -less" (lysnuth "lightless"). See Word formation.

context: Third-person pronouns mark animacy, not sex or gender, which suits a world of many races. sel is "he", "she" or singular "they".

personal.subject: dyn
personal.gloss: you, your (several; polite to one in Starisund)

rules.title: Personal pronouns
rules.rule: Pronouns have subject, object and possessive forms. The object forms change the vowel (em/om, dy/du, sel/sal), an old vowel alternation. Possessives come before the noun and replace the definite suffix.

rules.title: Polite you (Starisund)
rules.rule: In Auristar, speaking to a Light, a superior or a stranger of rank uses the plural dyn/dun/dyni. Common Norsund uses dy with everyone, which Aurinay find blunt.

examples.translation: O Light, will you guard our home?

rules.title: Reflexive and reciprocal
rules.rule: sjo "self" serves all persons; sjosjo means "each other".

examples.translation: Tyr sees himself in the water.

rules.title: Demonstratives take the definite suffix
rules.rule: hes "this" and thas "that" go before a noun that also carries the definite suffix (double definiteness).

rules.title: Question words and their family
rules.rule: Question words start with ku- (kum "who", kut "what", kur "where", kuna "when", kuvi "why", kuso "how", kumik "how much/many", kul "which"). Adding ynku-, neku- or alku- gives "some-", "no-" and "every-" words. kuna also means "when" as a conjunction.

rules.title: Dummy subject
rules.rule: Weather and other subjectless verbs take at "it" as a dummy subject, because a main clause needs something before the verb (V2).

context: Verbs do not agree with the subject. One present form serves every person, as in Norwegian and Swedish.
Every verb's dictionary form (infinitive) ends in -a after a consonant. The stem is the infinitive minus -a.

weak.imperative_epenthesis: e (added when the bare stem would end in a cluster that is not a legal coda: wandra > wandre!)

rules.title: Regular (weak) verbs
rules.rule: Present -er, past -ade, participle -ad, present participle -ande, command = bare stem. If the bare stem would end in a cluster that is not a legal coda (grammar/01), the command adds -e: wandra > wandre!, sundra > sundre!.

rules.title: Strong verbs
rules.rule: About twenty old, frequent verbs change their vowel in the past (ablaut) and take -en in the participle, in five classes: I i-ei-i, II u/y-au-o, III e-a-o, IV o-u-o, V a-o-a. Their present is regular (-er). New verbs are always weak.

rules.title: To be
rules.rule: vesa is irregular: present es, past vas, participle vesen. The present es is dropped in the carved style (mottos, inscriptions, verse) and in short exclamations.

examples.translation: Free the blade, bound the word.

rules.title: Future and conditional
rules.rule: hal + infinitive marks the future or a firm intention; halde + infinitive means "would".

examples.form: Sof em vas thiol, em halde rid-a.
examples.translation: If I were brave, I would ride.

rules.title: Perfect and pluperfect
rules.rule: aga "have" (present ager, past og) + participle.

rules.title: Progressive
rules.rule: vesa + present participle (-ande) for an action in progress.

rules.title: Passive
rules.rule: vesa + participle; the doer, if named, follows ur "from, by".

examples.translation: The wall was guarded by Tyr.

rules.title: Wishes and blessings
rules.rule: ma + infinitive, usually with the subject after ma.

rules.title: Modal verbs
rules.rule: orka "can", noda "must", thursa "want", lofa "may (be allowed)" take a bare infinitive.

rules.title: Negation
rules.rule: In a main clause, ne comes right after the finite verb, or after the subject when the subject follows the verb. In a subordinate clause, ne comes before the verb. A prohibition is ne + bare stem.

examples.translation: Tyr does not guard the wall.
Beneath the star, no rune shines.

rules.title: Verbs from nouns
rules.rule: Any noun can become a weak verb by adding -a: sund "song" > sunda "to sing", lys "light" > lysa "to shine", rit "writing" > rita "to write", kjold "ward" > kjolda "to guard".

context: Norsund speakers mark how they know what they say. The marker is a particle at the end of the sentence, set off by a comma.
Each particle grew out of an ordinary word (grammaticalization), which is how real grammar forms.

particles.meaning: so it is sung; I heard it
so the stars say; it is fated

rules.title: Three particles
rules.rule: sa (witnessed), sund (heard, reported, sung) and stari (foretold, fated). Without a particle a statement is plain assertion. Only one particle per sentence; it scopes over the main clause.

examples.translation: Tyr guarded the wall. (I saw it.)
Tyr guarded the wall. (So the songs say.)
Tyr will guard the wall. (It is foretold.)

rules.title: Where they are required
rules.rule: Oaths and court testimony take sa; testimony without sa counts as hearsay in an Auristar court. Prophecies, star-readings and temple decrees end in stari. A Sundwanderen song opens with the formula "Sund!" and its narrative lines take sund. Everyday speech uses them freely.

rules.title: In questions
rules.rule: In a question, the particle asks about the listener's source.

examples.translation: Who guarded the wall — did you see it yourself?

rules.title: Dialect preferences
rules.rule: Starisund speakers favour stari (it is fated); Vilnayan speakers favour sund (it is sung); Vilkyren reports favour sa. The Old Norsund register has no evidentials, which is why old oaths sound strangely bare to modern ears.

rules.title: Verb second (V2)
rules.rule: In a main statement the finite verb is always the second element. The first slot can hold the subject, an object, an adverb or a phrase; whatever is put first, the subject moves after the verb. Basic order is subject, verb, object, then adverbials (manner, place, time).

examples.translation: Tyr guards the wall at night.
At night, Tyr guards the wall.
The wall, Tyr guards. (context and animacy show who guards whom)

rules.title: Questions
rules.rule: Yes/no questions put the verb first. Questions with a ku- word put that word first and the verb second. Answers: hel "yes" (literally "good, whole"), ne "no".

rules.title: Subordinate clauses
rules.rule: Subordinate clauses do not use V2: subject, then negation (ne), then verb. They are introduced by ke "that", sof "if", kuna "when", ter ke "because", for ke "before", aft ke "after", thon "than".

examples.form: Em skyn-er ke Tyr ne kjold-er mur-in.
examples.gloss: 1SG know-PRS COMP Tyr NEG guard-PRS wall-DEF
examples.translation: I know that Tyr does not guard the wall.

rules.title: Relative clauses
rules.rule: A relative clause follows its noun and starts with ke "who, which, that" (a Kedre loan). The relativized noun leaves a gap; for a possessor, a resumptive possessive is used.

examples.translation: the free sword who guarded the wall
the free sword whose blade broke

rules.title: Noun phrase order
rules.rule: Determiner or possessor, number, adjective, noun, prepositional phrase, relative clause. A genitive possessor takes the determiner slot.

examples.form: hes thrim aur star-en i nett-in
examples.gloss: this three silver star-PL.AN in sky-DEF
examples.translation: these three silver stars in the sky

rules.title: Coordination
rules.rule: eth "and", ava "but", vo "or". "Both ... and" is eth ... eth; "either ... or" is vo ... vo.

rules.title: Emphasis (cleft)
rules.rule: To focus a phrase, use es + phrase + ke + clause.

examples.translation: It is Tyr who guards the wall.

rules.title: Existence
rules.rule: "There is" uses es with the place first (V2) or at as a dummy subject.

examples.translation: There is a rune in the wall.

rules.title: Prepositions
rules.rule: Norsund has prepositions only: i "in", a "on, at", ve "to, toward", ur "out of, from, by", fjol "under, beneath", mar "above, over", hjo "with, beside", ter "for", thurg "through", ymb "around", mid "among, amid", for "before", aft "after", ute "outside", inn "into". The full list is in dictionary/00-grammar-words.yaml.

rules.title: Evidentials at the edge
rules.rule: An evidential particle closes the sentence after everything else, set off by a comma (see Evidentials).

context: Most Norsund vocabulary is built from a few hundred roots with the affixes below and with compounding.
Contributors coining a new word should first try to build it from existing roots.

suffixes.meaning: lands or holdings of a folk

morphology.zero_derivation: Any noun can be used as a weak verb with -a; any adjective can be used as a noun with noun endings.

rules.title: Compounds are head-final
rules.rule: The last element is the head and decides class and meaning; earlier elements modify it.

rules.title: The linking -i-
rules.rule: When the first element owns or contains the second, a linking -i- (the old genitive) joins them: Stari-fjolden "the stars' under-land", Aur-i-star "star of silver light", Stari-sund "the star-tongue".

rules.title: Demonyms
rules.rule: Take the first element of the place name and add -nay. Thiolden > Thiolnay, Auristar > Aurinay, Oudeheim > Oudenay, Midelmar > Midelnay, Farheim > Farnay. A one-element name adds -nay directly.

rules.title: Agent nouns and the old -er
rules.rule: The living agent suffix is -ir (smidir "crafter", thjarkir "tracker"). A handful of old agent nouns keep the dead Old Norsund suffix -er: wander "wanderer" (as in Sundwanderen), kjolder "sentry".

rules.title: Kennings
rules.rule: A kenning names a thing by a two-part image: a base word plus a modifier, often with -i-. Kennings can nest (Snorri allowed up to five parts). Bards use them in place of plain nouns; see Poetics.

rules.title: The two -a suffixes
rules.rule: -a makes adjectives from nouns (Vilnay > Vilnaya) and also turns nouns into verbs (sund > sunda). Context and the dictionary decide; a coined word should use only one reading, and the dictionary lists which.

rules.title: Checklist for coining a word
rules.rule: 1. Can existing roots and affixes express it? 2. If not, pick a new root that passes the phonotactic checker and is not a real word in a major language or a slur. 3. Mark its layer (native, kedre) and epoch. 4. Submit as a pull request (docs/languages/norsund/contributing-words.md).

context: Norsund counts in tens. Old Vilnayan markets also reckon in the "long hundred" of 120 (langhaun).
Seven is sacred in Auristar (Seven Lights, seven-pointed star, the Council games every seven years for seven days).

morphology.compound: Larger numbers read largest first, without 'and': 523 = thammhaun dovtamm thrim
morphology.thousands: N mork: 523,208 = thammhaun dovtamm thrim mork, dovhaun ath
morphology.ordinal_rule: cardinal + -de (after voiced sounds) or -te (after voiceless); 'first' is ura; Starisund 7th is stevde

rules.title: Hand and five
rules.rule: thamm means both "hand" and "five". Ten, tamm, is a contraction of Proto-Norsund *dov-thamm "two hands". These are common real-world origins for number words.

rules.title: Sacred seven
rules.rule: In Starisund, sev "seven" became stev, reshaped by star (as English "female" was reshaped by "male"). The Seven Lights are Stevlysen; individual Lights are Lys Ura, Lys Dovde, Lys Thrimde, Lys Veste, Lys Thamde, Lys Seskte and Lys Stevde.

rules.title: Counting nouns
rules.rule: A number before a noun takes the plural (except yn).

rules.title: Titles put the ordinal after
rules.rule: Normally ordinals come before the noun (thrimde kreth "third ring"); in titles they follow (Lys Thrimde, the Third Light).

rules.title: Years
rules.rule: Vairean dates are read as numbers with ar "year": ar dovtamm sev aft Vaire (27 a.v.e), ar thrimhaun thammtamm for Vaire (350 b.v.e). Auristar also counts years from the fall of the star (90 a.v.e): ar yn aft Stardul.

context.This is the \"naming language\": enough rules and parts for any contributor to name people, places and groups consistently.

context: The tools/norsund name generator reads the place_generics and modifiers blocks below.

rules.title: Place names
rules.rule: A place name is modifier(s) + one generic, written as one word, stress on the first syllable: Nor + skyl = Norskyl ("North Falls"). Use the linking -i- when the modifier owns the place: Stari + fjol + den. Keep names to three syllables where you can; four is the limit for everyday names.

rules.title: Demonyms and peoples
rules.rule: First element + -nay for the people of a place (Thiolnay, Aurinay, Oudenay). -an for the lands of a people (Vilnayan). -myr for a god-blessed tribe (Nurmyr, Kullmyr). Plurals of peoples take -en (Runmyren).

rules.title: Personal names
rules.rule: A full name is given name + parent-name + optional byname. The parent-name is a parent's given name + -ung ("child of"), for any gender: Astrid Alkreggung, "Astrid, Alkregg's child". Many Farheim given names are inherited and have no known meaning (Astrid, Haakon). New given names are usually one or two name elements: Vim + tyr = Vimtyr.

rules.title: Bynames
rules.rule: A byname follows the name and carries the definite suffix: Eify Dunkstarin ("Eify the Darkstar"), Dethiol Dauthnuthin ("Dethiol the Deathless"). In English prose, give the byname in English on first mention and Norsund in dialogue: "Vimtyr, the Whispering Axe".

rules.title: House names
rules.rule: Noble houses of Auristar are named after a founder + -ungen ("the children of X"). Members use the house name after the parent-name. The founders of the Seven Wandering Houses are not yet named in canon.

rules.title: Titles
rules.rule: Titles come before the name: Lys "Light" (a member of the Seven Lights, with an ordinal: Lys Thrimde), Kyr "Blade" (a sworn mercenary rank: Kyr Thor'Vale), drott "ruler", vard "warden". A title used to address someone takes the Starisund vocative -a: Lysa!

rules.title: Names from other peoples
rules.rule: Kedre names (Rechtar, Vaire, Luxis), dwarven names (Karhak'Modan) and others keep their own forms and rules. Norsund speakers often make their own versions of foreign names: Luxis is Lysmar in Norsund.

rules.title: Translation convention for lore writers
rules.rule: Keep established Norsund proper names in English prose (Thiolden, Kjoldmur, Vilkyren). Translate titles and epithets into English in narration on first use and keep Norsund in dialogue, inscriptions and songs. Never mix a Norsund name with an English plural: write "the Vilkyren", not "the Vilkyrs".

rules.title: Renames for names that collided with other works
rules.rule: Valinor (Tolkien's Undying Lands) becomes Valnor, "north Valia" in Norsund (Val + nor). Worgenkin (Warcraft's worgen) becomes Ulfkin, "wolf-kin". Exeter and Arbury (real English towns) become the Kedre names Exaire and Arbaire. These renames were applied to the lore records on 2026-11-19.

context: Big cities innovate and isolated places conserve. Auristar's speech therefore changes fastest; Farheim and the countryside keep older forms.

context.Three high registers sit above everyday: Old Norsund (oath, law, liturgy, runes), learned Kedre (scholarship, imperial law) and bardic verse.

dialects.name: Common Norsund
dialects.speakers: Vilnayan towns and most of Thiolden; the second language of most races

dialects.name: Starisund ("star-tongue")
features: Stars, constellations and the Auristar are animate (staren, sel).
Seven is stev; the Seven Lights are Stevlysen.
Venetian-style accent: th is [s], final n is [ŋ], double consonants are short (spelling unchanged).
Plural dyn/dun/dyni is polite for one person.
Many Kedre loans in trade, law, building and canals (merk, kamp, port, tur, rie).

dialects.name: Farheim island speech
dialects.speakers: the island of Farheim and its emigrants
features: Most conservative; keeps some Old Norsund -in plurals (Vilkyrin) and the old present -ur in songs.

dialects.name: Kullmyr speech
features: y becomes i (Fyren > Firen, the Fire god; kyr > kir).
Runes are animate (runen), because the Kullmyr treat them as living.

dialects.name: Nurmyr speech
features: Initial h is dropped (heim > eim), which other speakers find rustic.

dialects.name: Thieves' cant
dialects.speakers: the Thieves Guild of Auristar and black-market traders

features.Backslang: a word's letters are reversed when legal (merk > krem "market", kyr > ryk "blade", vard > drav "warden").

features: Unratified slang lives in the sandbox tier of the dictionary.

registers.name: Old Norsund (archaic register)
registers.use: oaths, law, temple liturgy, rune-craft, sagas
registers.note: Full Old Norsund grammar is in records/languages/old-norsund/old-norsund.yaml. No evidentials.

registers.name: Learned register
registers.use: Starlight Library scholarship, alchemy, medicine, imperial law
registers.note: Pristine Kedre loans with Kedre stress (alkimia, medikina).

registers.name: Bardic verse (sundlag)
registers.note: Kennings, heiti and alliteration. See grammar/14-poetics.yaml.

registers.name: Carved style

rules.title: Doublets
rules.rule: The same Kedre root borrowed twice gives a worn-down everyday word and a learned one: tur "tower" (occupation) and turra "fortress-tower" (learned, in military treatises).

context: Family tree: Proto-Valian (deep past, all of Valia) splits into Proto-Norsund (Farheim) and Kedre (Keras, the Vairean heartland). Proto-Norsund > Old Norsund (settlers, 450 b.v.e.; rune slates) > Norsund (c. 100 a.v.e. onward), which splits into common Norsund, Starisund and other dialects.
Kedre and Norsund are distant cousins, as Latin and the Germanic languages are. Lysmar and Luxis are true cognates.
The rules below are machine-readable. tools/norsund applies them in order and its tests check that every cognate set comes out right.

Rule notation: env is a space-separated pattern. _ is the changing segment, # a word edge, V C F L N are categories, [a b] is a set, ? optional, + one or more, * zero or more. A rule with `unless` does not apply where that pattern matches.

morphological_history: Old Norsund animate plural -in and present tense -ur became -en and -er by the reduction rule (Vilkyrin > Vilkyren, kjoldur > kjolder).
Umlaut plurals (lud/lyd) come from a Proto-Norsund plural *-iz that triggered umlaut and was then lost.
Ten (tamm) is a contraction of *dov-thamm 'two hands'.
The evidential sa is the past tense of saja 'see'; sund is the noun 'song'; stari is the genitive of star.
ilin keeps its i because the vowel was long in Old Norsund (iliin): reduction only hit short vowels, and the long vowel shortened afterwards.
Starisund stev 'seven' is sev reshaped by star (contamination, not a regular sound change).
Dethiol, the Kullmyr leader's name, is Old Norsund *dauth-thiol 'brave unto death' worn down in Kullmyr speech.

rules.title: Why kyr has no kj
rules.rule: Palatalization (k > kj before front vowels) happened before umlaut created the y of kyr (*kuri > *kyri > kyr). By the time the vowel was front, the k-rule was over. Rule order explains the exception, as it does in real languages.

rules.title: Time depth
rules.rule: About 575 documented years separate the settlers (450 b.v.e.) from Auristar's walls (124 a.v.e.). Old Norsund is therefore hard but partly readable for modern speakers, roughly as Chaucer is for English speakers.

context: The Sundwanderen (song-wanderers) carry news across Thiolden in verse. Their measure is the sundlag ("song-law").

rules.title: The sundlag line
rules.rule: A line has two half-lines with two stressed syllables each, separated in writing by a raised dot. The first stressed syllable of the second half-line must alliterate with one or both stressed syllables of the first half-line. All vowels alliterate with each other. sk, st and sp alliterate only with themselves. Unstressed syllables are free.

rules.title: Heiti
rules.rule: Heiti are single poetic synonyms that exist only in verse, usually Old Norsund words: jor "steed" for hest "horse", bran "blade" for kyr, ljom "radiance" for lys. They are marked register poetic in the dictionary.

lines.gloss: test-PTCP seven-ORD salt sulphur and ash rune be.PRS.3PL mix-PTCP
lines.translation: Seventh experiment: salt, sulphur and rune-ash are mixed.

lines.text: Etera kurre per runa, kando runa es kalido.
lines.morphemes: etera kurr-e per runa kando runa es kalido
lines.gloss: aether flow-PRS.3SG through rune when rune be.PRS.3SG hot
lines.translation: Aether flows through the rune when the rune is hot.

lines.text: Eno fiala krepito runa rumpe porta.
lines.morphemes: eno fiala krepito runa rump-e porta
lines.gloss: one flask powder rune break-PRS.3SG gate
lines.translation: One flask of rune powder breaks a gate.
But the ash of the dead does not sleep.
Never mix the rune with water!

notes: The fourth line foreshadows what happened at Marheim, where the dead rose from the rune-blasted walls.
runa is a Norsund loan in Kedre (KED-REL-03); native runo only means "secret".

texts.title: Hymn to Luxis
texts.source: new (the Church of Light, records/thiolden/general-timeline.yaml, Year 0 a.v.e.)
texts.context: Sung at dusk in the houses of the Domo Luxis, the Church of Light, whose first priest is the Emperor. Every wish is in the subjunctive and the hymn closes with "Sik sia" (KED-REG-02).

lines.translation: Luxis, light above the night,

lines.text: luxia sangia Vaire ed kada nahi.
lines.morphemes: lux-ia sangia Vaire ed kada nahi
lines.gloss: bless-SBJV.SG bloodline Vaire and every nation
lines.translation: bless the bloodline of Vaire and every nation.

lines.text: Ke dia tue ardia in ardo,
lines.morphemes: ke dia tue ard-ia in ardo
lines.translation: May your day burn on the altar,

lines.text: ed fauto no tenia anime nostre.
lines.morphemes: ed fauto no ten-ia anim-e nostre
lines.translation: and may death not hold our souls.
So be it.

notes: In Norsund the goddess is Lysmar, "the High Light"; the two names come from the same Proto-Valian root.

texts.title: Doir Vaire's proclamation to the Vilnayan towns
texts.source: records/thiolden/general-timeline.yaml (Year 51 a.v.e., Doir Vaire is left in charge of the Vilnayan towns)
texts.context: Proclaimed in every Vilnayan town square when Rechtar's campaign ended and his daughter Doir became regent (reiato). Its words for market, gate and tribute are the ones Norsund borrowed (merk, port).

lines.text: Juba Doir Vaire, reiato Keria, a vike vili Thiolden:
lines.morphemes: jub-a Doir Vaire rei-ato Keria a vik-e vili Thiolden
lines.gloss: command-PRS.3SG Doir Vaire king-PTCP Keria to town-PL free Thiolden
lines.translation: Doir Vaire, regent of the Empire, commands the free towns of Thiolden:
The war is over; peace is born.

lines.text: Kada vika paga tributo a Keras, ed Keria gelda vike.
lines.morphemes: kada vika pag-a tributo a Kera-s ed Keria geld-a vik-e
lines.gloss: every town pay-PRS.3SG tribute to crown-DIGN and Keria shield-PRS.3SG town-PL
lines.translation: Every town pays tribute to Keras, and the Empire shields the towns.

lines.text: Merkadui ed porte son aperto a merkadari Keria.
lines.morphemes: merkadu-i ed port-e son aperto a merkad-ar-i Keria
lines.gloss: market-PL and gate-PL be.PRS.3PL open to market-AGT-PL Keria
lines.translation: Markets and gates are open to the merchants of the Empire.

lines.text: Kai ke tene runa kontra Keria, vole esere kvandato.
lines.morphemes: kai ke ten-e runa kontra Keria vole esere kvand-ato
lines.gloss: who REL hold-PRS.3SG rune against Keria FUT be.INF banish-PTCP
lines.translation: Whoever holds runes against the Empire will be banished.

lines.text: Aro tammo dekre ed eno post Keria.
lines.morphemes: aro tammo dekr-e ed eno post Keria
lines.gloss: year five ten-PL and one after Keria
lines.translation: Year fifty-one after Keria.

notes: merkadu keeps the old camp ending -u everywhere (court Kedre has no -o form of it); its plural is merkadui.
The vike vili, "free towns", translate Norsund Vilnayan, "lands of the free folk".

texts.topic: Sample texts from the v0.1 proposal
context: The first texts written in Norsund, kept as the canonical examples of the grammar. Each one shows a feature in use.

texts.title: Toast at Winterbeard's Sigil
texts.context: The standard toast of Auristar's taverns, raised when a round arrives. In Auristar the stars are living beings, so they take the animate plural staren.

lines.text: Kjal, thiolen! Ma staren kjolda dun.
lines.morphemes: kjal thiol-en ma star-en kjold-a dun
lines.translation: Drink, brave ones! May the stars keep you.

notes: In a Vilnayan tavern the stars are objects: Ma starar kjolda dun.
thiolen is the adjective thiol 'brave' used as a noun, so it takes the people-plural -en (ADJ-03).

texts.title: The Vilkyr code
texts.context: The motto every Vilkyr carves on the hilt of a first blade. It is the first line of the Vilkyr oath, in modern form.

lines.translation: Free the blade, bound the word.

notes: Carved style: the present copula is left out (ADJ-02, VERB-03).
vil and vothen alliterate on v, as in all bardic verse (POET-01).

texts.title: Gate inscription of the Kjoldmur
texts.source: records/thiolden/auristar/auristar.yaml (the city is prohibited from using runic magic)
texts.context: Carved over every gate of the First Ring. A charged rune glows, so "no rune shines" bans rune magic, not rune writing.

lines.translation: Beneath the star, no rune shines.

notes: Verb second: the phrase fjol starin comes first, so the subject run follows the verb, and ne follows the subject (SYN-01, VERB-10).

texts.title: The Prophecy of the Auristar
texts.context: The vision given to the leaders of the seven Wandering Houses of Oudeheim. It is recited in the temples of Auristar in this modern form; the immovable star is the Norstar, which fell on Midelmar in 90 a.v.e.

lines.text: Thiark aur star ke ne vyrner.
lines.morphemes: thiark aur star ke ne vyrn-er
lines.gloss: seek.IMP silver star REL NEG move-PRS
lines.translation: Seek a silver star that does not move.

lines.text: Thal doler sel, thal hjald dyni heim.
lines.morphemes: thal dol-er sel thal hjald dyni heim
lines.translation: Where it falls, there raise your home.
So the stars say.

notes: The star is sel 'she/he', not at 'it': in temple speech it is a living being (NOUN-09).
In the relative clause ke ne vyrner, ne comes before the verb (VERB-10).
Thal ... thal ('there ... there') pairs two clauses in place of a word for 'where'.
Prophecies end in stari (EVID-02).

texts.title: Three ways of knowing
texts.context: The same statement with each evidential particle (EVID-01).

lines.translation: Tyr guarded the wall. (I saw it.)
Tyr guarded the wall. (So the songs say.)
Tyr will guard the wall. (It is foretold.)

texts.title: Verb second
texts.context: The finite verb stays in second place whatever comes first (SYN-01, SYN-02).

lines.translation: Tyr guards the wall at night.
At night, Tyr guards the wall.
Do you guard the wall?

context: Two texts that conlangers translate so languages can be compared side by side. Both are adapted to Valia where a literal version would not make sense in-world.

texts.title: The Babel text (Genesis 11:1-9), adapted
texts.source: Genesis 11:1-9 (the Babel text, proposed as a conlang test by Jeffrey Henning in 1996)
texts.context: Retold as a Valian myth of why the peoples of Valia speak many tongues. The tower reaches for the sky, and the god who comes down is Nett, the Firmament, whose realm the tower threatens.

lines.text: Lang og al lyd yn sund eth sam sundar.
lines.morphemes: lang og al lyd yn sund eth sam sund-ar
lines.gloss: long.ago have.PST all person.PL one tongue and same word-PL.IN
lines.translation: Long ago all people had one tongue and the same words.

lines.text: Kuna lydene wandrade ur austin, hyttade selen slaun, eth thal thurmade selen.
lines.morphemes: kuna lyd-ene wandr-ade ur aust-in hytt-ade selen slaun eth thal thurm-ade selen
lines.gloss: when person.PL-DEF.PL.AN roam-PST from east-DEF find-PST 3PL.AN plain and there settle-PST 3PL.AN
lines.translation: When the people wandered from the east, they found a plain, and there they settled.

lines.text: Selen mal ve sjosjo: Heia, ma emen smida grjot ur lerv eth gylla at helt!
lines.morphemes: selen mal ve sjosjo heia ma emen smid-a grjot ur lerv eth gyll-a at hel-t
lines.gloss: 3PL.AN say.PST to RECP hey OPT 1PL make-INF stone from clay and bake-INF 3SG.IN good-ADV
lines.translation: They said to each other: Come, let us make stone out of clay and bake it well!

lines.text: Thana mal selen: Heia, ma emen hjalda burd eth tur, ke ati tyr tagger nettin!
lines.morphemes: thana mal selen heia ma emen hjald-a burd eth tur ke ati tyr tagg-er nett-in
lines.gloss: then say.PST 3PL.AN hey OPT 1PL raise-INF city and tower REL 3SG.IN.POSS point touch-PRS sky-DEF
lines.translation: Then they said: Come, let us build a city and a tower whose point touches the sky!

lines.text: Ma emen smida orth ter sjo.
lines.morphemes: ma emen smid-a orth ter sjo
lines.translation: Let us make a name for ourselves.

lines.text: Thana dul Nett ur nettin eth sa burdin eth turin.
lines.morphemes: thana dul Nett ur nett-in eth sa burd-in eth tur-in
lines.gloss: then fall.PST Nett from sky-DEF and see.PST city-DEF and tower-DEF
lines.translation: Then Nett came down from the sky and saw the city and the tower.

lines.text: Nett mal: Se, selen es yn nay, eth al ager sam sund.
lines.morphemes: Nett mal se selen es yn nay eth al ag-er sam sund
lines.gloss: Nett say.PST see.IMP 3PL.AN be.PRS one folk and all have-PRS same tongue
lines.translation: Nett said: Look, they are one people, and all have the same tongue.
Now they can make anything.

lines.text: Ma em dola eth skerva seleni sund.
lines.morphemes: ma em dol-a eth skerv-a seleni sund
lines.translation: Let me go down and change their tongue.
So they will not understand each other.

lines.text: Sva skervade Nett al lydi sund, eth selen drestade ur burdin ve al alden.
lines.morphemes: sva skerv-ade Nett al lyd-i sund eth selen drest-ade ur burd-in ve al alden
lines.gloss: thus change-PST Nett all person.PL-GEN tongue and 3PL.AN leave-PST from city-DEF to all world
lines.translation: So Nett changed the tongue of all people, and they left the city for every part of the world.

lines.text: Turin vas nekuna ulmad, eth emen skyner ne sjosjo til yt.
lines.morphemes: tur-in vas nekuna ulm-ad eth emen skyn-er ne sjosjo til yt
lines.gloss: tower-DEF be.PST never end-PTCP and 1PL understand-PRS NEG RECP until now
lines.translation: The tower was never finished, and to this day we do not understand each other.

notes: Present tense with future meaning: Sva skyner selen ne sjosjo (VERB-04 allows the plain present for near future).
dola 'to fall, descend' covers 'come down'; Nett falling from the sky echoes the Stardul, the Fall of the Star.
Purpose clauses ('to see the city') are avoided; Norsund chains verbs with eth instead.
The Lord of Genesis becomes Nett because Valia's gods live in the night sky (records/thiolden/auristar/auristar.yaml, Religion).

texts.title: The North Wind and the Sun
texts.source: Aesop, 'The North Wind and the Sun' (the International Phonetic Association's standard sample text)
texts.context: Told in the Vilnayan towns as a children's fable. The wind and the sun are personified, so they are animate (sel).

lines.text: Norbrys eth Sauv brakkade ymb kum vas thrakugar.
lines.morphemes: Norbrys eth Sauv brakk-ade ymb kum vas thrakug-ar
lines.gloss: north.wind and sun fight-PST about who be.PST strong-CMPR
lines.translation: The North Wind and the Sun were quarrelling about which of them was stronger.

lines.text: Thana leid yn wander i dalg kap.
lines.morphemes: thana leid yn wander i dalg kap
lines.gloss: then come.PST one wanderer in warm cloak
lines.translation: Then a wanderer came by in a warm cloak.

lines.text: Selen mal: Sel ke ura henser wanderi kap, es thrakugar.
lines.morphemes: selen mal sel ke ura hens-er wander-i kap es thrakug-ar
lines.gloss: 3PL.AN say.PST 3SG.AN REL first take-PRS wanderer-GEN cloak be.PRS strong-CMPR
lines.translation: They said: The one who first takes the wanderer's cloak is the stronger.

lines.text: Thana brysade Norbrys hjo al seli thrak.
lines.morphemes: thana brys-ade Norbrys hjo al seli thrak
lines.gloss: then blow-PST north.wind with all 3SG.AN.POSS strength
lines.translation: Then the North Wind blew with all its strength.

lines.text: Ava wanderin kromade seli kap ymb sjo.
lines.morphemes: ava wander-in krom-ade seli kap ymb sjo
lines.gloss: but wanderer-DEF hold-PST 3SG.AN.POSS cloak around REFL
lines.translation: But the wanderer held the cloak tight around himself.
At last the North Wind gave up.

lines.text: Thana lysade Sauv ur holvin, eth snar hans wanderin seli kap.
lines.morphemes: thana lys-ade Sauv ur holv-in eth snar hans wander-in seli kap
lines.gloss: then shine-PST sun from sky-DEF and soon take.PST wanderer-DEF 3SG.AN.POSS cloak
lines.translation: Then the Sun shone from the sky, and soon the wanderer took off his cloak.

lines.text: Sva nodade Norbrys mela ke Sauv vas thrakugar.
lines.morphemes: sva nod-ade Norbrys mel-a ke Sauv vas thrakug-ar
lines.gloss: thus must-PST north.wind say-INF COMP sun be.PST strong-CMPR
lines.translation: So the North Wind had to admit that the Sun was the stronger.

notes: Norbrys and Sauv are written with capitals because the fable treats them as persons; as ordinary nouns they are norbrys and sauv.
The comparative of thrakug 'strong' is thrakugar (ADJ-04).
hjo 'with' takes the possessive phrase al seli thrak 'all its strength'.
After a fronted adverb (thana, til ulm, snar) the subject follows the verb (SYN-01).

context.Texts as they are spoken, sung and carve: oaths, songs, laws, market talk, verse, watch calls, news and blessings.

texts.title: The Vilkyr oath (modern Norsund)
texts.source: records/thiolden/vilnayan.yaml (the Vilkyren's code); Old Norsund version in records/languages/old-norsund/texts.yaml
texts.context: Sworn by a new Vilkyr, hand on blade, before two witnesses. Most guild halls still use the Old Norsund wording; this modern version is used in Vilnayan towns that have no oath-keeper who knows the old tongue. An oath requires sa.

lines.translation: Free the blade, bound the word.

lines.text: Em vether a kyr eth a thamm.
lines.morphemes: em veth-er a kyr eth a thamm
lines.gloss: 1SG swear-PRS on blade and on hand
lines.translation: I swear on blade and on hand.

lines.text: Ter Thiolden, ter heim eth nay, kjolder em.
lines.morphemes: ter Thiolden ter heim eth nay kjold-er em
lines.gloss: for Thiolden for home and folk guard-PRS 1SG
lines.translation: For Thiolden, for home and folk, I keep watch.

lines.text: Skrimmin thiarker em, eth em vysker ne.
lines.morphemes: skrimm-in thiark-er em eth em vysk-er ne
lines.translation: The monster I hunt, and I do not flee.

lines.text: Emi kyr biter sal ke es vond.
lines.morphemes: emi kyr bit-er sal ke es vond
lines.translation: My blade bites the one who is evil.

lines.text: Ur eth Nett es emi sajiren, sa.
lines.morphemes: Ur eth Nett es emi sajir-en sa
lines.gloss: Ur and Nett be.PRS 1SG.POSS witness-PL.AN EVID.SEEN
lines.translation: Ur and Nett are my witnesses, as I see them.

lines.text: Sof em brester vethin, ma emi kyr bita om.
lines.morphemes: sof em brest-er veth-in ma emi kyr bit-a om
lines.gloss: if 1SG break-PRS oath-DEF OPT 1SG.POSS blade bite-INF 1SG.OBJ
lines.translation: If I break the oath, may my blade bite me.
Thus I swear, before witnesses.

notes: Compare the Old Norsund oath: it has cases and no evidentials, so it calls the gods as witnesses instead of using sa.
Line 4 puts the object first (skrimmin) and the subject after the verb (SYN-01).
Line 7: after a fronted if-clause, ma takes the verb-second slot (VERB-08).

texts.title: Kilia's song for Winterbeard's Sigil
texts.context: The bard Kilia's song, sung every time she visits Winterbeard's Sigil (Jalkvyrski Sjen) in the Fourth Ring of Auristar. This is a sung translation: it keeps the meaning and the eight-line shape, not the English rhymes.

lines.translation: Come, travellers, near and far,

lines.text: lid ve Jalkvyrski Sjen, kur aul es i kerin.
lines.morphemes: lid ve Jalkvyrsk-i sjen kur aul es i ker-in
lines.gloss: come.IMP to Winterbeard-GEN sigil where ale be.PRS in jug-DEF
lines.translation: come to Winterbeard's Sigil, where the ale is in the jug.

lines.text: Fyrin es dalg, aulin es kjeldug,
lines.morphemes: fyr-in es dalg aul-in es kjeldug
lines.gloss: fire-DEF be.PRS warm ale-DEF be.PRS cold
lines.translation: The fire is warm, the ale is cool,
and the stories are never dull.

lines.text: Bast kjalar hytter dy i denin,
lines.morphemes: bast kjal-ar hytt-er dy i den-in
lines.translation: The best drinks in the land you'll find here,
served by the kindest hands.

lines.text: Lid, kjal hjo omen, eth lemb yn drypling,
lines.morphemes: lid kjal hjo omen eth lemb yn drypling
lines.gloss: come.IMP drink.IMP with 1PL.OBJ and stay.IMP one moment
lines.translation: Come, drink with us, and stay a while,

lines.text: eth del dyni frastar, morkvod aft morkvod.
lines.morphemes: eth del dyni frast-ar morkvod aft morkvod
lines.gloss: and share.IMP 2PL.POSS story-PL.IN mile after mile
lines.translation: and share your tales, mile after mile.

notes: Line 5 fronts the object (bast kjalar) for emphasis, so the subject dy follows the verb (SYN-01).
themm 'hands' is an umlaut plural of thamm (NOUN-03).
Kilia addresses a crowd, so she uses the plural dyni 'your'.

texts.title: Laws of the Kjoldmur
texts.source: records/thiolden/auristar/auristar.yaml (the rune-magic ban; the rings of the Kjoldmur)
texts.context: Carved in the gatehouse of the Fifth Ring, where the city's courts sit. The Old Norsund formula above the First Ring gate (records/languages/old-norsund/texts.yaml) is older; these are the common-tongue laws every citizen is expected to know.

lines.translation: Beneath the star, no rune shines.

lines.text: Sel ke sjoler run i burdin, hal vesa skarnad.
lines.morphemes: sel ke sjol-er run i burd-in hal ves-a skarn-ad
lines.gloss: 3SG.AN REL charge-PRS rune in city-DEF FUT be-INF punish-PTCP
lines.translation: Whoever charges a rune with aether in the city shall be punished.
Testimony without sa is hearsay.

lines.text: Al kivid kjolder Kjoldmurin, eth Kjoldmurin kjolder al kivid.
lines.morphemes: al kivid kjold-er Kjoldmur-in eth Kjoldmur-in kjold-er al kivid
lines.gloss: every citizen guard-PRS Kjoldmur-DEF and Kjoldmur-DEF guard-PRS every citizen
lines.translation: Every citizen guards the Kjoldmur, and the Kjoldmur guards every citizen.

lines.text: I nimin ganer nekum thurg portin.
lines.morphemes: i nim-in gan-er nekum thurg port-in
lines.gloss: in night-DEF go-PRS nobody through gate-DEF
lines.translation: At night, no one passes through the city gate.
Thus is the law.

notes: Line 2: the whole subject sel ke sjoler run i burdin comes first, then the verb (SYN-01).
Line 3 is the rule behind EVID-02: in an Auristar court, testimony must carry sa.

texts.title: Haggling on a canal boat
texts.context: A pot-seller on a rieskei (canal boat) in the Fourth Ring and a citizen leaning over the quay. Both use the polite plural dyn, as Aurinay do with strangers. The seller ends a price with stari, a joke every Auristar market knows.

lines.speaker: seller
lines.text: Lys dyn! Hes kjelin es fjelg eth helt smidad.
lines.morphemes: lys dyn hes kjel-in es fjelg eth hel-t smid-ad
lines.gloss: light 2PL this pot-DEF be.PRS beautiful and good-ADV make-PTCP
lines.translation: Light to you! This pot is beautiful and well made.

lines.speaker: buyer
lines.text: Eth dyn lys. Kumik metter at?
lines.morphemes: eth dyn lys kumik mett-er at
lines.translation: And light to you. How much is it?

lines.speaker: seller
lines.translation: Four silver pennies, as the stars decree.

lines.speaker: buyer
lines.text: Ves? At metter ful myk! Dov.
lines.morphemes: ves at mett-er ful myk dov
lines.translation: Four? That's far too much! Two.

lines.speaker: seller
lines.text: Dov? Ne. Thrim, eth dyn henser ok lagelin.
lines.morphemes: dov ne thrim eth dyn hens-er ok lagel-in
lines.gloss: two no three and 2PL take-PRS also flask-DEF
lines.translation: Two? No. Three, and you take the flask as well.

lines.speaker: buyer
lines.text: Thrim eth lagelin? Hel, ma emen merka!
lines.morphemes: thrim eth lagel-in hel ma emen merk-a
lines.gloss: three and flask-DEF yes OPT 1PL trade-INF
lines.translation: Three and the flask? Yes, let's deal!

lines.speaker: seller
lines.translation: Thanks! May the stars keep you.

lines.speaker: buyer
lines.translation: Farewell!

notes: Starisund accent: the seller says [ˈsta.rəŋ] and [duŋ] (PHON-10).
Starkjold 'farewell' is the blessing ma staren kjolda du worn down to one word.

texts.title: Praise of the Seven Lights (sundlag)
texts.source: records/thiolden/auristar/characters/ (Tyr, Ulf, Haakon, Othil); the Third Light's death
texts.context: A praise poem sung on the steps of the Starirauggheim on Stardulvelth, the Feast of the Fall of the Star. Each line has two half-lines (·); the first stressed word of the second half alliterates with a stressed word of the first (POET-01).

lines.translation: Hear the song!

lines.text: Stevlysen ur ljomin · lyser ymb kvitburdin,
lines.morphemes: stev-lys-en ur ljom-in lys-er ymb kvitburd-in
lines.gloss: seven-light-PL.AN from radiance-DEF shine-PRS around white.city-DEF
lines.translation: The Seven Lights from the radiance · shine around the white city,

lines.text: selen kjolder starigandar, · kjoldar i kyrsundin.
lines.morphemes: selen kjold-er starigand-ar kjold-ar i kyrsund-in
lines.translation: they guard the star-roads, · shields in the blade-song.

lines.text: Tyr, hyrski tyr, · trammer for fylkin;
lines.morphemes: Tyr hyrsk-i tyr tramm-er for fylk-in
lines.gloss: Tyr spear-GEN point march-PRS before host-DEF
lines.translation: Tyr, the spear's point, · marches before the host;

lines.text: Ulf i ritheimin, · ura i skyn;
lines.morphemes: Ulf i ritheim-in ura i skyn
lines.gloss: Ulf in library-DEF first in knowledge
lines.translation: Ulf in the library, · foremost in knowledge;

lines.text: Haakon hjo nettkraft · heler al skeng;
lines.morphemes: Haakon hjo nettkraft hel-er al skeng
lines.gloss: Haakon with sky.power mend-PRS all pain
lines.translation: Haakon with the sky's power · heals every pain;

lines.text: Othil, oude sundir, · orth ur aftorvin;
lines.morphemes: Othil oude sund-ir orth ur aftorv-in
lines.gloss: Othil old sing-AGT renown out.of past-DEF
lines.translation: Othil, the old singer, · renown from times past;

lines.text: Thrimde Lys i nettin · thiolast mid staren.
lines.morphemes: thrim-de lys i nett-in thiol-ast mid star-en
lines.gloss: three-ORD light in sky-DEF brave-SUPL among star-PL.AN
lines.translation: The Third Light in the heavens · bravest among the stars.
Thus I have sung, as the stars decree.

notes: Alliteration: Stevlysen/ljomin with lyser (l); kjolder with kjoldar (kj); Tyr with trammer (t); Ulf, ura (vowels alliterate); Haakon with heler (h); Othil, oude, orth (vowels); Thrimde with thiolast (th).
Kennings: kvitburd 'white city' (Auristar), starigand 'star-road' (canal), kyrsund 'blade-song' (battle), hyrski tyr 'the spear's point' (Tyr).
The Third Light, killed by Dethiol, is praised as having transcended (stara) into the night sky.
Praise poems for the Lights close with stari instead of sund (POET-04).

texts.title: Watch call of the Nimkjold
texts.context: Cried from the walls of a Vilnayan town at each night hour, after three strokes on the gong (klemb).

lines.translation: Here is the Night Guard! The third hour of the night!

texts.title: The Vilkyr oath
texts.context: Sworn by every Vilkyr (free sword) on taking up the hunt, hand on blade, before two witnesses. The oath is still sworn in Old Norsund. Its first line is the Vilkyr code, which Norsund keeps as "Vil kyrin, vothen sundin".

lines.translation: Free blade, bound word.

lines.text: Em vethur a kyre eth a thamme.
lines.morphemes: em veth-ur a kyr-e eth a thamm-e
lines.gloss: 1SG.NOM swear-PRS.SG on blade-DAT and on hand-DAT
lines.translation: I swear on blade and on hand.

lines.text: Ter Thioldene, ter heime eth nege, kjoldur em.
lines.morphemes: ter Thiolden-e ter heim-e eth neg-e kjold-ur em
lines.gloss: for Thiolden-DAT for home-DAT and folk-DAT guard-PRS.SG 1SG.NOM
lines.translation: For Thiolden, for home and folk, I keep watch.

lines.text: Skryma thiarkur em, eth em ne skrinkur.
lines.morphemes: skrym-a thiark-ur em eth em ne skrink-ur
lines.translation: The monster I hunt, and I do not flee.

lines.text: Kyr emi bitur thasa ys vond es.
lines.morphemes: kyr emi bit-ur thas-a ys vond es
lines.gloss: blade 1SG.GEN bite-PRS.SG that.one-ACC REL evil be.PRS.SG
lines.translation: My blade bites the one who is evil.

lines.text: Sajir es Myr, sajir es Heid.
lines.morphemes: saj-ir es Myr saj-ir es Heid
lines.gloss: see-AGT be.PRS.SG Myr see-AGT be.PRS.SG Heid
lines.translation: Myr is witness, Heid is witness.

lines.text: Sof em vath brestur, biti kyr emi om.
lines.morphemes: sof em vath brest-ur bit-i kyr emi om
lines.translation: If I break the oath, may my blade bite me.
Thus I swear.

notes: There are no evidential particles; Old Norsund calls the gods as witnesses instead (line 6).
The accusative -a on skrym lets the object come first in line 4 without ambiguity.
Subordinate clauses put the verb last (sof em vath brestur, ys vond es).
The curse in line 7 uses the optative with the verb first.

texts.title: Law formula of the Kjoldmur
texts.context: Carved beside the gates of the First Ring of the Kjoldmur (built 91-99 a.v.e.). Auristar was founded after Old Norsund had given way to Norsund, but law is written in the old register. The formula bans rune magic (a charged rune glows), not rune writing.

lines.translation: This is the law of the Kjoldmur.

lines.text: Kum ys lysande run fjol stare ristur, thas es utlag.
lines.morphemes: kum ys lys-ande run fjol star-e rist-ur thas es ut-lag
lines.gloss: who REL shine-PRS.PTCP rune beneath star-DAT carve-PRS.SG that.one be.PRS.SG outside-law
lines.translation: Whoever carves a shining rune beneath the star, that one is outlaw.

lines.text: Kjold eth grith halur mur vesa.
lines.morphemes: kjold eth grith hal-ur mur ves-a
lines.gloss: ward and sanctuary owe-PRS.SG wall be-INF
lines.translation: Ward and sanctuary the wall shall be.

lines.text: Kum ys mur ne kjoldur, ne kjoldur heim.
lines.morphemes: kum ys mur ne kjold-ur ne kjold-ur heim
lines.gloss: who REL wall NEG guard-PRS.SG NEG guard-PRS.SG home
lines.translation: Whoever does not guard the wall does not guard home.
Thus we judge, the judges of the Kjoldmur.

notes: The genitive follows its noun (lag Kjoldmuri), as is usual in law language.
halur + infinitive is the old future; Norsund hal comes from it.
Kjoldmur contains the Kedre loan mur. The name is younger than true Old Norsund and is used here as a fixed name.

texts.title: A settlers' rune slate from Marheim
texts.context: A slate carved in the first years of Marheim, when the surviving settlers were raising the village in northern Thiolden. It is not the Merfolk slate the Mad Chronicler reads in records/user-submitted-stories/marv.yaml; Merfolk runes are a separate tradition. The rune-row does not mark vowel length or double consonants, so the reading below is a scholar's normalization.

lines.text: Yn hwander ristade runar hesar aft brode seli, ys i Norvire dul.
lines.morphemes: yn hwander rist-ade run-ar hes-ar aft brod-e seli ys i Norvir-e dul
lines.gloss: one wanderer carve-PST.SG rune-PL.IN this-PL.IN after sibling-DAT 3SG.GEN REL in North.forest-DAT fall.PST.SG
lines.translation: A wanderer carved these runes in memory of their sibling, who fell in the North-forest.
We are raising Marheim.
May Myr guard the home and the wanderers.

notes: The formula "X carved these runes after Y" is the standard memorial opening.
The demonstrative follows the noun (runar hesar), an old word order.
hwander keeps the initial hw that Norsund simplified to w (wander).

texts.title: Temple invocation to Myr and Heid
texts.source: records/thiolden/general-timeline.yaml (57 a.v.e., the blessings of Myr and Heid)
texts.context: Opening words of the oldest rite of Auristar's temples, from the years of the Seven Wandering Houses. It uses the old names Myr and Heid for Ur and Nett. In modern Starisund temple speech the same lines are followed by stari.

lines.translation: I call upon Myr and Heid.

lines.text: Myr, ur ys emin lidum; Heid, ve ys emin ganum.
lines.morphemes: Myr ur ys emin lid-um Heid ve ys emin gan-um
lines.gloss: Myr out.of REL 1PL.NOM come-PRS.PL Heid toward REL 1PL.NOM go-PRS.PL
lines.translation: Myr, from whom we come; Heid, to whom we go.

lines.text: Jov omum thioleth, jov omum lys.
lines.morphemes: jov omum thiol-eth jov omum lys
lines.translation: Give us courage, give us light.

lines.text: Kuna dauth lidur, marlidim emin ve Heide.
lines.morphemes: kuna dauth lid-ur mar-lid-im emin ve Heid-e
lines.gloss: when death come-PRS.SG high-come-OPT.PL 1PL.NOM toward Heid-DAT
lines.translation: When death comes, may we rise to Heid.
So is fate.

notes: Myr is the god of origin and kin, Heid of the sky and the destination, matching Ur and Nett.
marlida "rise, ascend" describes the triumphant dead joining the constellations (starmyr).
urlag "fate" is literally "origin-law".

texts.title: A memorial stone from the Haugden
texts.context: A long-branch rune stone raised beside a barrow on the Haugden, the tumulus plains, around 200 b.v.e. It follows the standard memorial formula (ON-NAME-02). The last line forbids anyone to charge the runes: rune magic near the dead raises them, a fear the fall of Marheim in 50 a.v.e. proved right.

lines.text: Ulf eth Sauvdis ristadum runar hesar aft Aurhaske, thade selini.
lines.morphemes: Ulf eth Sauvdis rist-adum run-ar hes-ar aft Aurhask-e thade selini
lines.gloss: Ulf and Sauvdis carve-PST.PL rune-PL.IN this-PL.IN after Aurhask-DAT father.DAT 3PL.AN.GEN
lines.translation: Ulf and Sauvdis carved these runes in memory of Aurhask, their father.

lines.text: Sel dul i strithe a Haugdene.
lines.morphemes: sel dul i strith-e a Haugden-e
lines.translation: He fell in battle on the barrow plains.

lines.text: Thiol lud vas sel, eth hel ter nege seli.
lines.morphemes: thiol lud vas sel eth hel ter neg-e seli
lines.gloss: brave person be.PST.SG 3SG.AN.NOM and good for folk-DAT 3SG.AN.GEN
lines.translation: A brave man he was, and good to his people.
May Myr keep his soul.
This barrow we raise.

lines.text: Ne lysi run a stave hese.
lines.morphemes: ne lys-i run a stav-e hes-e
lines.gloss: NEG shine-OPT rune on stave-DAT this-DAT
lines.translation: Let no rune shine on this stone.

notes: Read in long-branch runes, the carving does not mark the double consonants of Ulf's and Aurhask's kin; this is the scholars' normalization.
The verb agrees with its plural subject (ristadum, hjaldum).
The object comes first in line 5 and the verb stays second (V2).
The closing line is a protective curse in the optative, verb first, with ne before it.

texts.title: The landfall (from the Saga of the Wanderers)
texts.source: records/thiolden/general-timeline.yaml (450 b.v.e., the first settlers arrive from Farheim)
texts.context: The opening of the saga the Sundwanderen still recite in Old Norsund: the settlers from the island of Farheim cross the sea and reach the land they name Thiolden. Sagas tell events in the past tense and quote speech with mal "said".

lines.translation: This is the tale of the wanderers.

lines.text: Ur Farheime gonum selin a hjaule, i ves skeium.
lines.morphemes: ur Farheim-e gon-um selin a hjaul-e i ves skei-um
lines.gloss: out.of Farheim-DAT go.PST-PL 3PL.AN.NOM on sea-DAT in four ship-PL.DAT
lines.translation: From Farheim they went out on the sea, in four ships.

lines.text: Thrusk skauv skeiar, eth hjaul vas vond.
lines.morphemes: thrusk skauv skei-ar eth hjaul vas vond
lines.gloss: storm push.PST.SG ship-PL.IN and sea be.PST.SG bad
lines.translation: Storm drove the ships, and the sea was cruel.

lines.text: A nyvde dage saum selin hjolm.
lines.morphemes: a nyv-de dag-e sa-um selin hjolm
lines.translation: On the ninth day they saw a shore.

lines.text: Vir hin vas dunk, eth skrymin beidum i vire.
lines.morphemes: vir hin vas dunk eth skrym-in beid-um i vir-e
lines.gloss: forest the be.PST.SG dark and monster-PL.NOM wait.PST-PL in forest-DAT
lines.translation: The forest was dark, and monsters waited in the forest.
But the wanderers did not flee.

lines.text: Thal mal drott selini: “Hes es den thiolini.”
lines.morphemes: thal mal drott selini hes es den thiol-ini
lines.gloss: there say.PST.SG ruler 3PL.AN.GEN this be.PRS.SG land brave-PL.GEN
lines.translation: Then their leader said: “This is the land of the brave.”

lines.text: Sva agur den hin thyn ati: Thiolden.
lines.morphemes: sva ag-ur den hin thyn ati Thiolden
lines.gloss: thus have-PRS.SG land the name 3SG.IN.GEN Thiolden
lines.translation: So the land has its name: Thiolden.

notes: Line 7 gives the canon meaning of Thiolden, "land of the brave"; den thiolini ("land of the brave ones") was compounded to Thiolden.
Strong past plurals add -um to the past stem (gonum, beidum); saja has the irregular plural saum.
Dative after every preposition (ur Farheime, a hjaule, i vire).
The saga never uses evidentials; the Sundwanderen add sund only when they retell it in Norsund.

texts.title: A law of the Marheim moot
texts.context: From the laws recited at the stemn (moot) of Marheim before its fall. It sets the blood-price, the rule of witnesses and the punishment for breaking the peace of the moot. Its witness rule is the origin of the Auristar requirement that testimony carry sa.

lines.translation: This is the law of the moot of Marheim.

lines.text: Kum ys luda valdur, thas jovur bot vo es utlag.
lines.morphemes: kum ys lud-a vald-ur thas jov-ur bot vo es ut-lag
lines.gloss: who REL person-ACC slay-PRS.SG that.one give-PRS.SG blood.price or be.PRS.SG outside-law
lines.translation: Whoever slays a person pays the blood-price or is outlaw.
The blood-price is a long hundred goats (120).

lines.text: Sak skilur stemn, eth dov sajirin vethum.
lines.morphemes: sak skil-ur stemn eth dov saj-ir-in veth-um
lines.gloss: case judge-PRS.SG assembly and two see-AGT-PL swear-PRS.PL
lines.translation: The moot judges the case, and two witnesses swear.

lines.text: Sajir ys ne sa, thas ne vethur.
lines.morphemes: saj-ir ys ne sa thas ne veth-ur
lines.gloss: see-AGT REL NEG see.PST.SG that.one NEG swear-PRS.SG
lines.translation: A witness who did not see does not swear.

lines.text: Kum ys grith i stemne brestur, thas halur ute Marheime gana.
lines.morphemes: kum ys grith i stemn-e brest-ur thas hal-ur ute Marheim-e gan-a
lines.gloss: who REL sanctuary in assembly-DAT break-PRS.SG that.one owe-PRS.SG outside Marheim-DAT go-INF
lines.translation: Whoever breaks the peace of the moot shall go out of Marheim.
Thus we judge, the judges of Marheim.

notes: Each rule is a relative clause with the verb last, then a main clause beginning with thas ("that one").
Line 3 counts in the long hundred and uses the umlaut plural get "goats".
Line 5 is the root of the Auristar court rule; in Norsund the past sa "saw" became the evidential sa.

texts.title: A ward incantation (rune magic, forbidden in Auristar)
texts.context: WARNING FOR WRITERS: this is rune magic. Spoken while charging (lada) carved ward-runes on a doorpost, it makes the runes glow. Rune magic raised the dead at Marheim and is forbidden in Auristar by the law of the Kjoldmur; a glowing rune inside the city is always a crime or a sign of forbidden magic. Plain runic writing never glows. The text comes from a Runmyren slate and follows the incantation shape of ON-REG-06.

lines.text: Run ristur em, run ladur em.
lines.morphemes: run rist-ur em run lad-ur em
lines.translation: A rune I carve, a rune I charge.

lines.text: Vald i grjote, sveim i stave.
lines.morphemes: vald i grjot-e sveim i stav-e
lines.gloss: arcane.field in stone-DAT aether.current in stave-DAT
lines.translation: Field in the stone, current in the stave.

lines.text: Lysi run hin i dunke nime.
lines.morphemes: lys-i run hin i dunk-e nim-e
lines.gloss: shine-OPT rune the in dark-DAT night-DAT
lines.translation: May the rune shine in the dark night.
May no wraith come to the home.

lines.text: Kjoldi run hin ylv eth fyr, luda eth gata.
lines.morphemes: kjold-i run hin ylv eth fyr lud-a eth gat-a
lines.gloss: guard-OPT rune the water and fire person-ACC and goat-ACC
lines.translation: May the rune guard water and fire, person and goat.
Glow!

notes: The final word seals the charge; at that moment the runes begin to glow.
vald and sveim are the two forces of magic in records/magic-rules.yaml (Arcane fields and Aether currents).
Animate objects take the accusative -a (luda, gata); inanimate ones do not (ylv, fyr).
Use this only for scenes of forbidden or wild magic, never as everyday Auristar practice.

context: Kedre ("the Tongue") is the language of the Vairean Empire, spoken in Keras and the old Kingdom of Reinovaire, north-west of Thiolden in Valnor.
It is a distant cousin of Norsund; both descend from Proto-Valian. Its sound history is the pv-kedre stage of records/languages/norsund/grammar/13-history.yaml.
It looks Latin to a reader on purpose, as the conquerors' language does in-world, but it has its own rules. This file is the complete 1.0 grammar.
Glosses follow the Leipzig Glossing Rules. DIGN = dignity suffix, AGT = agent, SBJV = subjunctive, Q = question particle.

dignity_suffix.meaning: marks a god, an emperor's title or a holy city

place_suffixes.form: ia,   meaning: "land of; also abstract domain", examples: [Keria "crown-land, the Empire", rivia "channel (land of running water)"]
aire, meaning: "domain, house of", examples: [Vaire, Reinovaire, Exaire, Arbaire]

other_suffixes.form: orio, meaning: "place where something is done", examples: [ardorio "furnace, alchemist's hearth", skriborio "chancery"]
ato,  meaning: "past participle; also the thing done", examples: [jubato "decree", probato "experiment"]
e,    meaning: "adverb from adjective", examples: [tele "bravely", alte "loudly"]

prefixes.form: ni,    meaning: "no- (negative pronouns)", examples: [nikai "no one", nikado "nothing", nikando "never"]

verbs.future: vole + infinitive (vole luxare 'will bless'); vole never changes
verbs.passive: esere + past participle (Marheim es obsidato 'Marheim is besieged')

numbers.tens: unit + dekre (plural of dekra): 20 fovo dekre, 70 sevi dekre
numbers.compound: tens + ed + unit: 27 fovo dekre ed sevi
numbers.hundreds: unit + kentie (plural of kenti): 300 trimi kentie; 100 is kenti
numbers.thousands: unit + mile (plural of mila): 2000 fovo mile; 1000 is mila
numbers.ordinals: primo 'first'; otherwise drop the final vowel and add -esmo: fovesmo, trimesmo, kvaresmo, tammesmo, sesesmo, sevesmo, attesmo, nevesmo, dekresmo
numbers.cognates: fovo, trimi, tammo and sevi share Proto-Valian roots with Norsund dov, thrim, thamm and sev (13-history cognates). eno, kvaro, sesi, atti, nevi and dekra are Kedre's own.

rules.title: Sounds
rules.rule: Kedre has the consonants p t k b d g f v s h m n l r j and the vowels a e i o u, with the diphthongs ai, au and ei. It has no th, no y, no kj or gj and no w (Proto-Valian w became v). Breathy stops became f at the start of a word and b or d inside it (bh, dh), and gh became h (rules k-breathy-initial, k-breathy-medial and k-gh in 13-history): Kedre fens "land" beside Norsund den, fovo "two" beside dov, geldo "shield" beside kjold.

rules.title: Stress
rules.rule: Stress falls on the second-to-last syllable: KE-ras, ke-RI-a, rei-no-VAI-re, al-ki-MI-a. Norsund kept this stress only in learned loans (alkimia, medikina, kupola).

rules.title: Word endings
rules.rule: Most words end in a vowel. Final consonants are limited to s, n and r (Keras, Luxis, fens, Rechtar, Doir). A Proto-Valian final u became o (rule k-final-u: *telu > telo). Court Kedre keeps that o; camp Kedre (KED-REG-04) still says u in many nouns (merkadu, kividu, denaru).

rules.title: Sound inventory
rules.rule: Consonants by place: lips p b f v m; teeth and ridge t d s n l r; palate j [j]; velum k g; throat h. The old name spelling cht stands for a rasping [xt], found only in Rechtar. Vowels are short; Proto-Valian long vowels shortened (rule k-length).

rules.title: Syllables and clusters
rules.rule: Syllables are (C)(C)V(C). Allowed onsets are any single consonant; a stop or f plus r or l (pr, br, tr, dr, kr, gr, fr, pl, bl, kl, gl, fl); s plus p, t or k; and kv (from Proto-Valian kw: kvandro). Inside a word a syllable may close on r, l, n, m or s, or on the first half of a double consonant (murra, legia has none, atti, osso). Words end in a vowel or in s, n, r. There is never more than one consonant at the end of a word.

examples.translation: window: three syllables, double n split, tr onset
wanderer: kv onset, n closing the first syllable

rules.title: Spelling
rules.rule: k is always written k (Keras, Keria), never c. x stands for ks (luxi, Luxis). j is the y-sound of "yes" (jubare). The old spelling cht, found only in names such as Rechtar, stands for [xt]. Double consonants are written double. There are no accents.

rules.title: Kedre names in Norsund lore
rules.rule: In English-language lore, Kedre names keep their Kedre spelling (Rechtar Vaire, Luxis, Reinovaire, Rundir Voidet). The adjective of Vaire is Vairean in English. Norsund speakers either keep a Kedre name (Keras) or replace it with their own word (Luxis is Lysmar). A Kedre name inside a Norsund compound keeps its capital.

rules.title: Nouns
rules.rule: Kedre nouns have no gender and no case. The plural changes the final vowel (posto > posti, legia > legie, kedre > kedri, luxi > luxie, merkadu > merkadui) or adds -es after a consonant (fens > fenses). There are no articles: a bare noun is "a" or "the" as context needs.

rules.title: Head-first compounds and genitives
rules.rule: The head comes first and the modifier or owner follows, the opposite of Norsund: reino Vaire "realm of Vaire" (written as one name, Reinovaire), sangia Vaire "the bloodline of Vaire", Domo Luxis "the House of Luxis" (the Church of Light).

rules.title: The dignity suffix -s
rules.rule: -s marks a deity, an imperial title or a holy city: luxi "light" > Luxis "Light (the goddess)", kera "crown" > Keras "the Crowned (city)". Norsund speakers translate the goddess as Lysmar instead of borrowing the name.

rules.title: Noun phrase order
rules.rule: Numbers and quantifiers (kada "every", toto "all", multo "many") come before the noun. Everything else follows it, in this order: adjective, demonstrative, possessive, owner: legia telo esto "this brave legion", luxi tue "your light", fovo legie Vaire "two legions of Vaire".

rules.title: Adjectives
rules.rule: Adjectives follow the noun and do not change (legia telo "a brave legion", legie telo "brave legions"). The comparative is plu before the adjective with ke "than"; the superlative takes the prefix supra-; adverbs change the final vowel to -e.

examples.translation: a legion braver than a nation

rules.title: Pronouns
rules.rule: me, te, se, nos, vos, sei serve as subject and object; possessives mue, tue, sue, nostre, vostre follow the noun (luxi tue "your light"). sui is the reflexive for every person; esto "this" and ilo "that" follow the noun.

rules.title: Verbs
rules.rule: Two classes, -are and -ire, with person endings in the present (luxo, luxi, luxa, luxamo, luxate, luxan). The past adds -av- or -iv- before the endings (luxava "blessed"). The participle ends in -ato or -ito and often serves as a noun: jubato "decree" (lit. "the commanded"). The future is vole + infinitive.

examples.translation: Luxis blessed the bloodline of Vaire.

rules.title: Full verb paradigms
rules.rule: Every regular verb follows one of the two tables below. The subjunctive (-ia, -ian) expresses wishes and blessings, and purpose after a ke "so that". The imperative is -a/-i for one person and -ate/-ite for several. The present participle (-ante, -ente) is an adjective: luxi luxante "shining light". The passive is esere + past participle.

rules.title: The verb esere "to be"
rules.rule: esere is the only irregular verb: present so, ses, es, somo, sete, son; past ero, eri, era, eramo, erate, eran; subjunctive sia, sian; imperative si; participle esito. "Sik sia" ("so be it") closes every prayer. vole, the future marker, never changes.

rules.title: Numbers
rules.rule: Cardinals: nulo 0, eno 1, fovo 2, trimi 3, kvaro 4, tammo 5, sesi 6, sevi 7, atti 8, nevi 9, dekra 10, kenti 100, mila 1000. Tens, hundreds and thousands are counted with the plural of the base word (fovo dekre 20, trimi kentie 300, fovo mile 2000); units follow with ed "and" (fovo dekre ed sevi, 27). Ordinals: primo, then -esmo (fovesmo, trimesmo ... dekresmo). fovo, trimi, tammo ("hand, five") and sevi are cognate with Norsund dov, thrim, thamm and sev.

rules.title: Negation
rules.rule: no comes right before the verb: "no vinka" "does not conquer"; "no luxa!" "do not bless!". The negative pronouns nikai "no one", nikado "nothing", nikando "never" take no other negation when they come first.

examples.translation: Night does not conquer the light of Vaire.

rules.title: Questions
rules.rule: A yes/no question starts with the particle ka and keeps statement order. A question word (kai who, kado what, kaube where, kando when, perkado why, kalo how, kanto how much, kaio which) comes first. Answers: si "yes", no "no".

rules.title: Word order
rules.rule: Everyday speech is subject-verb-object. Imperial decrees put the verb first (Juba Rechtar ... "Rechtar commands ..."). Negation is no before the verb.

rules.title: One word for every subordinate clause
rules.rule: ke introduces every subordinate clause: "that", "who", "which", and "than" after plu. Norsund borrowed it during the occupation and uses it for relative clauses and "that" clauses.

rules.title: Coordination and subordination
rules.rule: ed "and", sed "but", au "or", ned "nor". Subordinate clauses keep statement order and are introduced by ke or by a phrase ending in ke: si "if", perke "because", a ke "so that" (with the subjunctive), ante ke "before", post ke "after", kando "when", dum "while".

examples.translation: I command that the wall fall.
